source_context.creator: unknown from local visual alone
source_context.caption_hook: Forecasting, planning and buying are different jobs that jointly determine inventory performance.
caption_argument: Planning translates the signal into supply, capacity and inventory decisions.
Buying creates the cash and receipt commitment.
The operational problem is the delay and misalignment between those three functions.
observed_performance_context: Included in Tiger's intentionally curated Top-100 reference set.

reader_situation.primary_reader: Planner, buyer or inventory leader who sees forecast changes arrive after commitments have already been made.
reader_situation.work_moment: A cross-functional discussion has become vague because people use forecasting, planning and buying as if they were interchangeable.
reader_situation.tension: Everyone owns part of inventory performance, but no one can see where responsibility and financial exposure change hands.
reader_situation.topic_selection_boundary: This record does not choose a topic, terms, audience or future post angle.

attention_physics.thumbnail_read_0_3_seconds: Three large, adjacent labels—Forecasting, Planning and Buying—signal a distinction the reader likely feels but has not cleanly named.
attention_physics.comprehension_3_10_seconds: The repeated vertical structure lets the reader compare definition, role, inputs, outputs and success measure across all three without changing reading rules.
attention_physics.value_exchange_10_30_seconds: The reader acquires a vocabulary for diagnosing the forecast-to-plan-to-PO hand-off, not merely three definitions.
attention_physics.identity_or_curiosity_trigger: Operational people recognise the sentence-level conflict: 'the forecast changed' versus 'the order is already placed.'
attention_physics.promise_proved_by_visual: The equal columns prove that the three activities are related but non-identical; the graphic makes the boundary visible before the caption explains the consequence.

visual_forensics.asset_specific_observation: High-contrast three-column comparison table with repeated decision rows and a shared conclusion.
visual_forensics.composition_and_grid: A single-page comparison board: high-contrast title area above three equal vertical lanes. Each lane follows the same row order, with a dark category label at the top/side and a compact block of information below.
visual_forensics.dominant_anchor: The three-way comparison itself; no decorative hero image competes with it.
visual_forensics.hierarchy: Large functional labels create first-level scan; short descriptors and row labels create second-level scan; supporting details remain subordinate.
visual_forensics.typography: Bold high-contrast sans-serif labels, intentionally stronger than explanatory copy. This is a reading interface, not a poster.
visual_forensics.colour_material_and_contrast: Restrained white surface with dark anchors and separated lanes; colour is used for categorical separation rather than mood.
visual_forensics.imagery_role: Minimal. The visual primitive is a table/comparison, which is the proof mechanism.
visual_forensics.density_and_pacing: Fast entry, then controlled vertical reading. Repetition reduces cognitive switching despite a high information load.
craft_observations: The columns are genuinely comparable, not three unrelated text boxes.
The content is compressed into decision-relevant categories rather than encyclopaedic detail.
The reader can stop at any lane and still retain a complete local answer.

content_mechanics.primary_cognitive_job: Disambiguate related concepts so a group can make a more precise decision.
argument_sequence: connect misalignment to inventory and cash consequences
invite the reader to identify their own weakest link
content_mechanics.compression_method: Parallel schema: every concept answers the same small set of questions.
content_mechanics.reader_payoff: A reusable way to clarify accountability and escalation in a forecasting-to-buying process.
save_share_return_motives: Useful in a meeting where terms are being conflated
Easy to send to a planner/buyer counterpart
Acts as a concise onboarding reference
content_mechanics.caption_to_visual_choreography: The image handles the distinction; the caption supplies the operational consequence—forecast shifts, plan lag, order already placed—and turns the visual taxonomy into a live business problem.

mechanism_fingerprint.primary_cognitive_job: Disambiguate related concepts so a group can make a more precise decision.
information_grammar: separate each concept through the same questions
social_action_mechanics: use to make an abstract disagreement specific
use_when: The chosen opportunity contains a small set of terms readers mistake for one another.
Each term can be compared fairly on the same decision-relevant schema.
The payoff is a clearer boundary, owner, choice or escalation.
do_not_use_when: The core value depends on a chronological causal story.
The concepts are not genuinely comparable.
The post requires rich emotional recognition rather than precision.
mechanism_fingerprint.topic_selection_boundary: This mechanism chooses no topic, audience, terms or comparison rows. Those are selected only after opportunity research.

transferable_atoms: Start with three terms readers casually conflate.
Force each term through the same decision schema.
Use the final shared section to expose the failure at the hand-off, not within an individual function.
Let the caption provide a lived scenario the comparison itself cannot show.
recombination.reverse_build_specification: When a selected opportunity contains a small set of conflated concepts and needs a shared decision vocabulary, use equal comparison lanes to make the boundary visible in the first frame. Keep one repeated decision schema across all lanes, then reveal the hand-off or consequence that the separated concepts create together. Make the visual deliver precision; let the caption supply the lived scenario, nuance and invitation. Require accurate definitions and a real reason the distinction matters. Do not use this mechanism for a causal timeline or unrelated categories, and do not borrow the source's terms, wording, type system or lane construction.
editable_levers: number of concepts: two to four
required_original_inputs: Validated definitions from the target operating process
Named data owner for each concept
Real decision boundary or failure mode
Original examples or sourced process logic
recombination.falsification_question: If relevant readers cannot tell which date they own or what action changes when it moves after ten seconds, did the distinction transfer?
